Fixture 66: Anchor Positioning (one-canvas subset)

CSS Anchor Positioning one-canvas subset · absolute and fixed targets place against an in-scope anchor · font-family "Liberation Sans"

ANCHOR-POSITIONING

Audit of the eight anchor positioning properties plus @position-try. Each row states the contract and shows a live Effect demo with a real anchor and an absolutely positioned tip. The blinkless engine moves the tip against the anchor; engines without anchor support keep the ordinary absolute offsets. Scroll hiding is out of scope: anchor-visible matches anchor-valid on this canvas.

# Property What it should do Effect (live)
1 anchor-name
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Stores none or one or more dashed idents. Two boxes can carry different names and none clears the list. Invalid keeps the previous value.
--a
--b
tip --a
Tip names --a, so it sits above the left anchor. The --b anchor stays put.
2 anchor-scope: all
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		all hides every name on that element from descendants outside it. A target outside the scope behaves as if the anchor were missing.
in
outside
Tip is outside the scope, so it keeps its left/top offsets instead of moving.
3 anchor-scope: list
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		A name list hides only those names. Other names on the same element stay visible. Lookup only, no containing block.
2 names
shown
--hidden is scoped out, --shown still moves the tip above the anchor.
4 position-anchor
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Names one dashed ident. Unknown names keep the earlier valid value. An out-of-scope name behaves like a missing name.
menu
below
Tip sits below the menu anchor, start-edge aligned. Anchor does not move.
5 position-anchor: auto (single)
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		auto uses the anchor only when exactly one in-scope name exists. One anchor plus auto moves the tip.
only
auto
Exactly one name in scope, so auto resolves to it and the tip goes above.
6 position-anchor: auto (ambiguous)
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		With several in-scope names, auto does not guess. The box keeps its ordinary absolute offsets until an explicit name is given.
one
two
stays
Two names in scope, so auto keeps the left/top fallback near the bottom.
7 position-area: top
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Places the absolute tip in the cell above the anchor: smaller Y than the anchor, X aligned to the anchor start edge. Paint ops move with the box.
core
above
Core proof: tip Y above anchor Y, same start X. Anchor unmoved.
8 position-area: none, static
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		none keeps left and top offsets. A static box with position-area keeps its flow position and never moves.
none
static
stays in flow
Dangling name plus none keeps offsets; static box ignores the property.
9 position-try-fallbacks, order normal
longhands · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		First fallback runs only when the base fails visibility. With always the base wins. With normal the document order wins.
top-edge
falls right
Top spills above the stage and right spills past it, so no-overflow hides the tip in both engines.
10 position-try-order: most-inline-size
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Size keywords pick the largest passing no-overflow candidate on that axis. A wide candidate wins over a narrow one when both fit.
mid
wide wins
Both sides fit, so the wider geometry wins on the inline axis.
11 position-try, @position-try
shorthand plus at-rule · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		Shorthand expands to order plus fallbacks. A dashed ident reads the area stored on @position-try --above. Unknown idents are skipped.
at
at-rule
Fallback --above resolves to the stored top area above the anchor.
12 try-tactic flip-block
fallback tactic · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		A tactic flips the chosen area across its axis after the area is known and before the final shift. Flipped Y lands on the opposite side.
fl
below
fl
flipped
Plain bottom sits below; with the anchor near the bottom the base spills, so flip-block mirrors it above the anchor.
# Property What it should do Effect (live)
13 position-visibility: always, anchor-valid
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome yes
Chrome supported 		always keeps the base even off canvas with ops intact. anchor-valid with a dangling name keeps ordinary absolute placement and still paints.
edge
always
dangling
Always keeps paint intact; with explicit offsets the base is the fallback overlap. Dangling name falls back to left/top and paints.
14 position-visibility: no-overflow, anchor-visible
longhand · CSS Anchor Positioning · Chrome partial
Chrome partial: scroll hiding 		no-overflow rejects candidates outside the viewport. anchor-visible is stored but equals anchor-valid here: no scroll offset exists, so no scrollport hiding.
vis
visible
Same geometry as anchor-valid on this canvas. Scroll-linked hiding waits on host scroll work.
